name: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners PLC

profile.description: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners is the world's largest Coca-Cola bottler by revenue, producing, distributing, and selling Coca-Cola branded and other non-alcoholic beverages across Western Europe, Australia, the Pacific, and Indonesia. Serves approximately 600 million consumers across 31 countries with brands including Coca-Cola, Fanta, Sprite, Monster Energy, and Costa Coffee. Formed through the 2021 merger with Coca-Cola Amatil. Headquartered in Uxbridge, United Kingdom.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): CCEP completed the transformative acquisition of Coca-Cola Amatil in 2021, rebranding to Europacific Partners and expanding from a European bottler to a global operation spanning 31 countries — a significant strategic pivot that opened the Asia-Pacific growth vector and increased revenue from EUR 12B to EUR 20B+ [1]. Q1 2026 showed 6.7% revenue growth with volume up 1.6%, demonstrating successful integration. AI Deployment (1/2): CCEP has deployed AI across procurement analytics, an AI-powered Career Hub for global talent management, an internal AI academy, and AI-based demand forecasting across 31 markets — practical deployment with operational impact but no quantified revenue or cost savings publicly reported [3]. Market Share (2/2): World's largest Coca-Cola bottler by revenue with dominant market share in Western European beverage distribution and growing Asia-Pacific presence, serving 600 million consumers [1]. Product Pipeline (0/2): No specific next-generation product launches with defined timelines; growth driven by volume, mix, and pricing optimization within existing categories. R&D Intensity (1/1): Investment in AI analytics, digital supply chain transformation, and sustainability-focused packaging innovation (100% recyclable packaging targets) is above average for the bottling industry [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): CCEP's purpose of creating 'a better shared future' through sustainable beverages is clear and connects to environmental stewardship, but is broadly similar to other consumer goods companies' sustainability commitments and not deeply distinctive as a vision of a future state [4]. Community Impact (2/2): CCEP earned MSCI ESG Rating of AA, CDP Climate A List recognition nine consecutive years, ISS ESG Prime Rating of C+, and FTSE4Good constituent for ten years — demonstrating genuine, measurable environmental stewardship that is distinctive among beverage industry peers [5]. Over 25% of public float held by ESG-focused funds validates the commitment. Employee Retention (1/2): 'People join for the brands and stay for the people' messaging is supported by dedicated VP of Culture and Leadership with decade-long tenure and investment in AI-powered learning and development, but no specific retention or turnover data available to distinguish from well-run peers [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying by CEO Damian Gammell or other executives in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Q1 2026 delivered EUR 5.13B revenue (up 6.7% reported, 9.4% FX-neutral) with volumes up 1.6%, and the company reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of 3-4% revenue growth, ~7% operating profit growth, and comparable free cash flow of at least EUR 1.7B [1]. ROE of 22.89% comfortably exceeds the 15% target. Forward P/E of approximately 19.5 is near the 20 target. D/E of 141% reflects Amatil acquisition leverage but is being systematically reduced, scoring 0.69 against the 300% floor. Dividend metrics are strong: payout ratio of 47% is well-controlled, 10+ consecutive years of payments (2x weight), 8 consecutive years of growth, and approximately 18.4% 5-year dividend growth CAGR (2x weight) driven by post-Amatil expansion [6]. Profit margin of 9.29% is structurally constrained by the bottling model but typical for the industry. Liquidity easily cleared: ~1.86M avg vol x $106 = $197M daily.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Beverage bottling and distribution is a physical-world manufacturing and logistics operation that AI structurally cannot displace — producing, bottling, warehousing, and delivering billions of servings across 31 countries requires massive physical infrastructure including bottling plants, cold-chain logistics, and distribution fleets [1]. Exclusive bottling agreements with The Coca-Cola Company create contractual moats that AI cannot circumvent. Consumer beverage demand is non-discretionary and AI-immune. Increasing urbanization and warm weather trends may actually increase beverage consumption. The only AI risk is potential for AI-driven DTC or alternative distribution, but the physical infrastructure requirements make this implausible at scale. AI Opportunity (0/1): CCEP deploys AI internally for procurement analytics, demand forecasting, and talent management, generating operational efficiency gains, but no quantifiable AI-driven revenue products have been reported [3].

infinite_game.summary: CCEP demonstrates solid infinite game characteristics through sustained environmental stewardship (CDP Climate A List nine consecutive years), the transformative Amatil acquisition that reshaped the company for decades, and CEO Gammell's decade-long tenure providing strategic consistency. The exclusive partnership structure with The Coca-Cola Company creates natural long-term orientation, though the fundamentally execution-focused bottling model limits the depth of the Just Cause and the company has not faced the kind of existential test that validates truly infinite thinking.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): CCEP's purpose of creating 'a better shared future' through sustainable beverages is genuine and partially lived out, validated by nine consecutive CDP Climate A List awards, MSCI AA ESG rating, and FTSE4Good membership for ten years [5]. Strategic decisions — the Amatil acquisition, sustainability investments, 100% recyclable packaging targets — can be traced back to this cause. However, the cause has not been tested through existential crisis, and the primary business model (bottling sugary drinks) creates inherent tension with health and wellness aspects of a 'better shared future.'

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Dedicated VP of Culture and Leadership with decade-long tenure and investment in AI-powered talent development demonstrate organizational commitment to people [3]. CEO Gammell's tenure since 2016 provides leadership stability. 'People join for the brands and stay for the people' messaging is consistent. However, no standout evidence of exceptional psychological safety or dramatically above-average retention distinguishes CCEP from well-run consumer staples peers.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): CCEP operates within a Coca-Cola franchise system where competition is framed around operational excellence rather than rival destruction. Management acknowledges PepsiCo bottlers' strengths in specific markets and uses competitive benchmarking to improve distribution efficiency and execution rather than pursuing zero-sum competition [1]. The focus on earning the right to grow through better execution reflects an infinite competitive mindset.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The 2021 Coca-Cola Amatil acquisition was a significant strategic evolution — transforming from a European bottler to a global Europacific operation, entering Australia, New Zealand, Indonesia, and the Pacific [1]. This expanded the addressable market from 300M to 600M consumers and diversified geographic risk. However, the core business model (bottling and distributing Coca-Cola products) remained fundamentally unchanged — a geographic extension, not a business model reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Acquiring Coca-Cola Amatil during COVID-19 (2021) required significant financial commitment and integration risk, demonstrating willingness to invest for long-term positioning when market conditions were uncertain [1]. Sustained ESG investment resulting in AA MSCI rating and CDP A List status represents choosing long-term environmental stewardship over near-term cost optimization. However, no examples of dramatically sacrificing profitable but misaligned business lines distinguish CCEP beyond sound corporate stewardship.

investment_thesis: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners is the world's largest Coca-Cola bottler, offering defensive consumer staples exposure with improving profitability and growing shareholder returns. Q1 2026 delivered EUR 5.13B revenue (up 6.7% reported, 9.4% FX-neutral) with volume growth of 1.6%, driven by pricing, mix, and market share gains [1]. FY2026 guidance reaffirmed at 3-4% revenue growth, ~7% operating profit growth, comparable free cash flow of at least EUR 1.7B, and a EUR 1B share buyback. ROE of 22.89% demonstrates efficient capital allocation, and the exclusive bottling agreements across 31 countries serving 600 million consumers create a durable competitive moat with predictable cash flows. The MSCI AA ESG rating and CDP A List status for nine consecutive years attract ESG-focused capital (25%+ of float) [5]. At a forward P/E of approximately 19.5 with a 2.41% dividend yield growing at 18.4% CAGR over five years, CCEP offers an attractive total return profile for a defensive compounder.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on low organic growth and structural margin constraints. FY2026 revenue guidance of 3-4% falls below the company's own midterm 7% target, suggesting consumer volume headwinds in mature European markets from health-conscious consumption trends, sugar taxes, and GLP-1 weight-loss drug adoption potentially reducing caloric beverage demand [1]. D/E of 141% reflects Amatil acquisition leverage that constrains financial flexibility and increases interest expense sensitivity. Profit margin of 9.29% is structurally limited by the bottling model's high raw material costs (sugar, PET plastic, aluminum) and energy-intensive manufacturing — input cost inflation directly compresses margins. The PEG ratio of 2.79 suggests the stock may be overvalued relative to its modest growth trajectory. Currency risk is significant with operations across 31 countries and EUR-reported earnings but USD-priced shares, with BEUC greenwashing complaints about recyclability claims creating additional ESG-related reputational risk [5].
key_catalysts: Operating profit growth of ~7% outpacing 3-4% revenue growth in FY2026, demonstrating continued margin expansion from Amatil integration synergies and AI-driven operational efficiency gains [1]
EUR 1B share buyback program reducing share count and boosting per-share metrics on top of the 2.41% dividend yield with 18.4% five-year dividend growth CAGR [1]
Asia-Pacific volume growth in Indonesia and Australia providing a higher-growth offset to mature European markets as CCEP captures rising per capita Coca-Cola consumption in emerging economies
key_risks: Secular health-conscious consumer trends, sugar taxes, and GLP-1 weight-loss drug adoption potentially reducing caloric beverage demand in mature European markets, with 2026 revenue guidance of only 3-4% already below the midterm 7% target

Raw material and energy cost inflation — sugar, PET plastic, aluminum, and energy prices directly compress the structurally thin 9.29% profit margin with limited pass-through ability to large retailers
Currency translation risk across 31 countries with EUR-reported earnings and USD-priced stock creating earnings volatility, compounded by D/E of 141% increasing sensitivity to rising interest rates
